explanation: A possible late delivery is a risk because it may or may not happen. A refused permit that has stopped work is an issue because it exists now. A budget ceiling is a constraint. An expectation that the council will approve, without proof, is an assumption.

stem: On an agile team, how is work usually assigned during an iteration?
options: The sponsor approves each task before it begins
Team members select, or pull, tasks themselves
The product owner assigns tasks to each developer
The project manager assigns each task in advance
explanation: Agile teams are self-managing: members pull tasks from the iteration backlog based on priority and capacity. The product owner decides what is most valuable, not who does each task.

stem: A finance department processes the payroll on the last day of every month. How is this work best classified?
options: A project
A program
A portfolio
Operations
explanation: Monthly payroll is ongoing, repetitive work, which is operations. A project is temporary and creates a unique result; programs and portfolios are groupings of projects and other work.

stem: After explaining a change to a stakeholder, the project manager asks her to summarize what she understood. Which part of the communication model is this?
options: Encoding of the message by the person sending it
Feedback that confirms the message was understood
The medium that is used to transmit the message
Noise that interferes with the message being sent
explanation: In the sender-receiver model, the receiver decodes the message and the sender checks understanding through acknowledgment and feedback. Asking for a summary is a way to get that feedback.

stem: A team plans the next three months in detail but leaves later work at a high level until more is known. What is this technique called?
options: Fast tracking
Crashing
Rolling wave planning
Resource smoothing
explanation: Rolling wave planning is iterative planning in which near-term work is planned in detail and later work stays at a higher level until it gets closer. Fast tracking and crashing compress schedules, and smoothing adjusts resources within float.

skill: When to use an adaptive approach
stem: A start-up wants to learn whether restaurants will pay for its booking app before building the full product. It releases a simple version with only the booking feature to a few restaurants. What is this version called?
options: An information radiator
A definition of done
A minimum viable product
A work breakdown structure
explanation: A minimum viable product has just enough features to be used by real customers, so the team can test its assumptions and learn what to build next. The other terms are a scope breakdown, a quality standard for increments and a visible progress display.

stem: What should a business analyst usually do first when a new initiative is proposed?
options: Choose the software product the company should purchase
Understand the business problem or opportunity behind it
Write the detailed test cases for the planned solution
Set the release dates for every feature in the solution
explanation: Business analysis starts by understanding the need: the problem to solve or opportunity to pursue. Choosing products, writing tests and setting dates come after the need and requirements are understood.

stem: A roadmap is organized into three columns: Now, Next and Later. What is the main advantage of this format?
options: It lists every task with its exact start and finish date in the plan
It shows which team member is assigned to each of the features
It replaces the product backlog, so no backlog needs to be kept
It shows priorities without committing to exact dates far in the future
explanation: A Now, Next, Later roadmap shows the order of priorities and the level of certainty without promising precise dates for later work, which keeps it flexible. It does not replace detailed planning or the backlog.

stem: Which term describes the series of phases a project passes through from its start to its completion?
options: Project life cycle
Work breakdown structure
Product life cycle
Performance measurement baseline
explanation: The project life cycle is the series of phases a project passes through from start to completion. The product life cycle covers a product from concept through retirement and usually spans many projects.

stem: Two senior engineers disagree about a design. The project manager brings them together to explore both views and find a solution that meets both concerns. Which conflict resolution technique is this?
options: Smoothing, also called accommodating
Withdrawing, also called avoiding
Forcing, also called directing
Collaborating, also called problem solving
explanation: Collaborating incorporates multiple viewpoints to reach consensus and commitment, which often leads to a lasting win-win result. Forcing imposes one view, smoothing plays down differences, and withdrawing leaves the conflict unresolved.

stem: What can happen when a schedule is resource leveled?
options: The project's end date always moves earlier because resources are freed
The cost baseline is removed so that resources can be used as needed
The project's end date may move later and the critical path may change
The scope of the project is reduced to match the available resources
explanation: Resource leveling adjusts start and finish dates to balance demand with supply, which can extend the schedule and change the critical path. It does not cut scope or remove baselines.

stem: A team does not know enough about a new technology to estimate a story. It sets aside a short, timeboxed piece of work to research it. What is this called?
options: A sprint review
A release
A burnup
A spike
explanation: A spike is a short, timeboxed piece of research or experimentation used to reduce uncertainty so a story can be estimated or designed. It is not an event, a release or a chart.

stem: What does a requirements management plan describe?
options: The list of final requirements that the customer has approved so far
How requirements will be analyzed, documented, prioritized and managed
How the company will market the product once it has been released
Which developer will build each requirement and in what order of work
explanation: The requirements management plan describes how requirements will be analyzed, documented and managed, including prioritization, configuration management and traceability. The approved list itself is the requirements documentation.

stem: What is the purpose of release planning on an adaptive project?
options: To decide which features will go into an upcoming release and roughly when
To decide the hourly tasks each developer will do on each day of the sprint
To assign blame for features that were not delivered in the last release
To approve the budget for the whole product for the next five years
explanation: Release planning looks ahead several iterations to forecast which features or stories will be in a release and when, using velocity and priorities. Daily tasks are planned within sprints.

stem: A team member asks you not to mention a known defect in the status report so the release date is not questioned. What should you do?
options: Move the release date quietly without saying why it has been changed
Mention the defect only to the team, since stakeholders do not need detail
Leave the defect out of the report, since the team plans to fix it soon
Report the defect accurately and discuss the effect on the release date
explanation: The honesty standard asks practitioners to provide accurate and timely information. Hiding a known defect, even with good intentions, misleads stakeholders who rely on the report to make decisions.

stem: Which type of PMO directly manages and controls projects?
options: Supportive
Consultative
Directive
Controlling
explanation: A directive PMO takes control of projects by directly managing them, so its degree of control is high. A supportive PMO provides templates and lessons, and a controlling PMO requires compliance with frameworks and tools. Consultative is not one of the three PMO types PMI describes.

stem: In a start-to-start relationship between activities A and B, what is true?
options: B cannot finish until A has finished
B cannot start until A has started
B cannot start until A has finished
A cannot finish until B has started
explanation: Start-to-start means the successor cannot start until the predecessor has started, for example leveling concrete cannot start until pouring has started. The other options describe finish-to-start, finish-to-finish and start-to-finish.

stem: In Kanban, what does cycle time measure?
options: The time from when work starts on an item until it is done
The length of each sprint, agreed when the project starts
The number of items the team completes in each sprint
The time from when an item is requested until a sprint ends
explanation: Cycle time measures how long an item takes from the start of work to completion. Lead time runs from the request to delivery, throughput counts items completed, and Kanban does not require sprints.

stem: An analyst compares the company's checkout process with the processes of industry leaders to find ideas for improvement. Which technique is this?
options: Prototyping
Decomposition
Benchmarking
Interviewing
explanation: Benchmarking compares practices, processes or products with those of comparable organizations to find best practices and ideas for improvement. Prototyping builds a model, decomposition breaks work down and interviewing questions individuals.

stem: What does a gap analysis compare?
options: The planned budget with the actual budget spent
The current state with the desired future state
Planned value with earned value on the schedule
Two vendors' prices for the same product
explanation: Gap analysis compares the current state of a process, capability or product with the desired future state to identify what must change. Budget and earned value comparisons are cost and schedule controls.

stem: At the end of a project, where should its lessons learned be placed so that future projects can use them?
options: In the risk register of the next project the team starts
In the organization's lessons learned repository
In the project charter, before it is archived with the records
In the team's sprint backlog for the following sprint
explanation: At closing, the project's lessons learned register is transferred to the organization's lessons learned repository, an organizational process asset that future projects draw on. The charter, a later project's risk register and a sprint backlog are not where an organization keeps its knowledge.

stem: What does the Pareto principle, often called the 80/20 rule, suggest?
options: A small number of causes often produce most of the problems
Teams should spend 80 percent of their time planning work
Most projects finish with about 80 percent of their scope
About 20 percent of risks are positive opportunities
explanation: The Pareto principle states that a relatively small number of causes typically produce most of the problems or defects, so effort should focus on those vital few. The other statements are not what the principle says.

stem: What is the performance measurement baseline?
options: The quality metrics agreed with the customer for each of the deliverables
The list of key performance indicators set for each team member's review
The benchmark of other companies' results used to set project targets
The integrated scope, schedule and cost baselines used to measure performance
explanation: The performance measurement baseline integrates the scope, schedule and cost baselines and is used to compare actual performance, for example in earned value management.

skill: When to use an adaptive approach
stem: What is the difference between iterative and incremental development?
options: Iterative releases the product once at the end; incremental never releases it at all
Iterative requires a fixed contract; incremental requires the work to have no budget
Iterative is used only for hardware; incremental is used only for software projects
Iterative refines the product through repeated cycles; incremental adds usable pieces
explanation: Iterative development improves the product through repeated cycles of feedback and refinement, while incremental development delivers the product in usable additions. Many agile approaches combine both.

stem: An analyst describes a fictional user, "Maria, a 34-year-old nurse who orders supplies on night shifts", to help the team understand users. What is this called?
options: A persona
A user story map
A stakeholder register
A use case
explanation: A persona is a fictional character that represents a group of real users, with goals and behaviors, to help the team keep users in mind. A use case describes interaction steps, a story map arranges stories, and the register lists real stakeholders.

stem: An acceptance criterion reads: "Given a customer has items in the basket, when they apply a valid code, then the total is reduced." What style is this?
options: INVEST, a checklist for writing user stories
Given, when, then, from behavior-driven development
RACI, a chart of roles and responsibilities
MoSCoW, a technique for prioritizing requirements
explanation: The given, when, then format comes from behavior-driven development. It states the starting context, the action and the expected outcome, which makes acceptance criteria easy to test.

stem: Which activity belongs to closing a project or phase?
options: Estimating the duration of each planned activity
Creating the work breakdown structure for the work
Identifying stakeholders and issuing the charter
Archiving project records and releasing resources
explanation: Closing includes obtaining acceptance, transferring the product, archiving records, capturing final lessons and releasing team members and other resources. The WBS and estimates belong to planning; stakeholder identification and the charter belong to initiating.

stem: Which technique gathers opinions from experts anonymously in several rounds to reach consensus?
options: Nominal group technique
A focus group
The Delphi technique
A facilitated workshop
explanation: The Delphi technique uses anonymous, repeated rounds of expert input with a facilitator summarizing results, which reduces bias and undue influence. Focus groups, nominal group technique and workshops are face-to-face and not anonymous.

stem: A project has an earned value (EV) of \$36,000 and a planned value (PV) of \$40,000. What is the schedule performance index (SPI)? Type the number only, to one decimal place.
explanation: SPI = EV / PV = 36,000 / 40,000 = 0.9. The project has completed 90 percent of the work it planned to have done by now, so it is behind schedule.

stem: Partway through a sprint, the company cancels the product the sprint goal was meant to support. In Scrum, who has the authority to cancel the sprint?
options: The product owner
Any of the developers
The team's line manager
The Scrum Master
explanation: A sprint can be cancelled if its goal becomes obsolete, and only the product owner has the authority to cancel it. The Scrum Master and developers do not, and line managers are outside the Scrum team.

stem: After a workshop, what should the analyst do with the notes on what stakeholders said?
options: Remove any points that disagree with what the sponsor said before
Confirm them with the stakeholders to check they are accurate and complete
Send them straight to the developers so they can start building at once
File them away, since anything that was said in the room is already agreed
explanation: Elicitation results should be confirmed with stakeholders to make sure they were understood correctly before they are analyzed and used. Skipping confirmation risks building on misunderstandings.

stem: After the requirements on a predictive project have been baselined, a stakeholder wants to change one. What should happen?
options: The analyst edits the document directly and tells no one
The change goes through the project's change control process
The request is refused, since baselines can never change
The team builds both versions and lets the users choose
explanation: Baselined requirements can change, but only through change control so the impact on scope, schedule, cost and risk is assessed before a decision. Unrecorded edits and building both versions are poor practice.
